about: Research sheet for the District of Columbia edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files.
name: District of Columbia
phones_sentence: The veterans office phone, address and hours come from the Mayor’s Office of Veterans Affairs page.

offices.source_title: District of Columbia: Mayor’s Office of Veterans Affairs
offices.note: MOVA’s District Veteran Service Officers help with VA claims, pension, survivor benefits and District veterans programs at no charge.
offices.selection: Office address, phone and hours as printed on the MOVA page (read in full); staff names omitted. The page’s footer also shows 1350 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, Suite 332; the card uses the address under “Contact Us”.

list.address: One Judiciary Square, 441 4th St NW, Suite 707 North, Washington, DC 20001
list.hours: Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
list.note: District Veteran Service Officers help with federal VA claims and benefits; MOVA also takes requests through its online intake form.

aging.source_title: DC Department of Aging and Community Living: Agency contact
aging.source_scope: 500 K Street NE; phone (202) 724-5626; TTY 711; office hours Monday to Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; Adult Protective Services (202) 541-3950; search excerpt.
aging.agency_label: DC Department of Aging and Community Living
aging.description: The DC Department of Aging and Community Living (DACL) is the District’s aging agency and Aging and Disability Resource Center: information and help for residents 60 and older, adults with disabilities and caregivers, including senior centers, meals, transportation, in-home support and legal services.
aging.next_step_extra: TTY users dial 711. Office hours are weekdays 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

regions.label: District of Columbia
regions.name: DC Department of Aging and Community Living (DACL)
notes: Office: 500 K Street NE, Washington, DC 20002.

regions.name: Office of the D.C. Long-Term Care Ombudsman (Legal Counsel for the Elderly)
regions.source_title: Legal Counsel for the Elderly: The Office of the D.C. Long-Term Care Ombudsman
regions.source_scope: Phone 202-434-2190 and email; replies within 24 hours or the next business day; serves residents of nursing homes, assisted living and community residence facilities and people on the EPD Medicaid waiver at home; read in full; page updated July 15, 2024. The Attorney General’s elder justice brochure (https://oag.dc.gov/sites/default/files/2024-03/EJS-brochure-updated-08292023-.pdf; updated August 2023; search excerpt) lists 202-434-2140 instead.
notes: Email DCOmbuds@aarp.org. The Attorney General’s 2023 elder justice brochure lists 202-434-2140; the program’s own page gives 202-434-2190.

cils.source_title: ILRU: Directory of Centers for Independent Living, District of Columbia results
cils.scope: Each office’s phones; read in full. Addresses come from ILRU’s map directory (https://www.ilru.org/cil-directory/dc; search excerpt). The directory lists the District as “Washington” county.
cils.phone_label: Phone listed in the ILRU national directory of Centers for Independent Living

list.name: DC Center for Independent Living
list.organization: The DC Center for Independent Living (DCCIL)
notes: Main office: 2600 12th Street NE, Washington, DC 20018; TTY 202-388-0277.
Other offices: 2901 14th St NW, 202-280-6899; Anacostia, 2443 Good Hope Road SE, 202-889-5802.

programs.name: DC veterans: Mayor’s Office of Veterans Affairs for claims help
programs.organization: District of Columbia, Mayor’s Office of Veterans Affairs (MOVA)
programs.description: Free help with federal VA claims and benefits from MOVA’s District Veteran Service Officers, plus outreach, community resources and District veteran programs for veterans and their families.
programs.next_step: Call MOVA at 202-724-5454 (weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.) or use its online intake form.
constraints: Call ahead; the office is in One Judiciary Square.

sources.title: District of Columbia: Mayor’s Office of Veterans Affairs
sources.scope: Services, District Veteran Service Officers, address, phone and hours; read in full.

sources.title: MOVA: Veteran Claims Assistance
sources.scope: Claims help through MOVA’s District Veterans Service Officer; search excerpt.

programs.name: DC Department of Aging and Community Living (Aging and Disability Resource Center)
programs.organization: DC Department of Aging and Community Living (DACL)
programs.description: The District’s aging agency and Aging and Disability Resource Center: senior centers, meals, transportation, in-home support, caregiver help and legal services for residents 60 and older and adults with disabilities. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call DACL at 202-724-5626 (TTY 711), weekdays 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.
programs.phone_label: DC Department of Aging and Community Living (202-724-5626)

sources.title: DC Department of Aging and Community Living: Agency contact
sources.scope: Address, phone, TTY, office hours and the Adult Protective Services line; search excerpt.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (DC SHIP)
programs.organization: DC Department of Aging and Community Living, State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP)
programs.description: Free, unbiased health insurance counseling for Medicare beneficiaries, families and caregivers in the District from DACL’s SHIP counselors.
programs.next_step: Call the SHIP Helpline at 202-727-8370 or email ship.dacl@dc.gov. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: The helpline keeps limited weekday hours; leave a message if no one answers.

sources.title: DACL: Health Insurance Counseling (DC SHIP)
sources.scope: Free health insurance information and counseling for Medicare beneficiaries; phone (202) 727-8370; search excerpt.

sources.title: DACL: About SHIP fact sheet (2026)
sources.scope: SHIP Helpline (202) 727-8370, email ship.dacl@dc.gov, helpline hours; search excerpt.

programs.name: DC Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: Legal Counsel for the Elderly, Office of the D.C. Long-Term Care Ombudsman; DACL Adult Protective Services
programs.description: Advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and community residence facilities, and for people receiving EPD waiver services at home. Adult Protective Services takes reports of abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation of vulnerable adults, 24 hours a day.
programs.next_step: Call the ombudsman at 202-434-2190 or email DCOmbuds@aarp.org. To report abuse, call Adult Protective Services at 202-541-3950, 24 hours a day. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

sources.title: Legal Counsel for the Elderly: The Office of the D.C. Long-Term Care Ombudsman
sources.scope: Phone, email, response time and who the program serves; read in full.

sources.title: DC Office of the Attorney General: Elder Justice brochure (updated August 2023)
sources.scope: Report abuse by calling 911 or the Adult Protective Services 24-hour hotline, (202) 541-3950; Legal Counsel for the Elderly (202) 434-2120; search excerpt.

programs.name: Free legal help for older District residents
programs.description: Legal Counsel for the Elderly provides free legal help to older District residents. DACL also lists legal services for seniors among its programs.
programs.next_step: Call Legal Counsel for the Elderly at 202-434-2120, or ask DACL (202-724-5626) about legal services for seniors.
constraints: Legal aid screens by age, income and case type.

sources.title: DC Office of the Attorney General: Elder Justice brochure (updated August 2023)
sources.scope: Legal Counsel for the Elderly (AARP), (202) 434-2120; search excerpt.

sources.title: Legal Counsel for the Elderly: Senior Medicare Patrol
sources.scope: Legal Counsel for the Elderly: 202-434-2120; search excerpt.

programs.name: VA health care in the District
programs.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Washington DC Healthcare System
programs.description: District veterans are served by the Washington DC VA Medical Center, 50 Irving Street NW (202-745-8000), and its community clinics.
programs.next_step: Call 202-745-8000 for appointments; after hours, ask the operator for the administrator on duty. Not enrolled yet? Ask MOVA for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.

sources.title: VA Washington DC health care: Contact us
sources.scope: Washington DC VA Medical Center, 50 Irving Street NW; local 202-745-8000; search excerpt.
